full_description: Learn to transform existing architectural and interior models into compelling visual presentations with Twinmotion. Develop practical skills in importing 3D scenes, refining materials, creating natural and artificial lighting, adding landscapes and environmental assets, and preparing realistic architectural images. Build camera sequences and cinematic walkthroughs, explore day and evening presentation options, and deliver client-ready visual experiences using professional scene optimization, export and handover workflows.

commercial_differentiation.headline: Don't Just Show a 3D Model. Create an Architectural Experience.
commercial_differentiation.supporting_copy: A 3D model is not automatically a presentation. Real-time visualization requires controlling light, framing camera perspectives, curating realistic context, and balancing performance. Learn to build architectural presentations that communicate design intent faithfully rather than relying on gimmicky presets.

learning_outcomes: Understand Twinmotion's real-time visualization workflow and production role.
Navigate the Twinmotion interface, viewport, docks, and scene graph efficiently.
Configure suitable viewport quality and hardware settings for stable performance.
Import prepared 3D architectural models with correct units, orientation, and scale.
Use compatible Datasmith and Direct Link workflows for seamless geometry transfer.
Reimport and synchronize design updates when source models are modified.
Organize architectural geometry using containers, groups, and clear scene hierarchies.
Identify and resolve common material-import issues, missing textures, and UV distortions.
Apply realistic architectural materials from the built-in library (wood, concrete, glass, metal).
Understand physically based rendering (PBR) properties: roughness, metallic, normal, and opacity.
Configure natural daylight, sun position, elevation, and atmospheric exposure.
Create evening and artificial-light scenarios using interior fixtures, spotlights, and IES lights.
Use HDRI environments for realistic environmental illumination and reflections.
Control dynamic weather, cloud cover, rain, seasons, and time-of-day settings.
Understand Lumen real-time global illumination and indirect bounce lighting concepts.
Utilize built-in vegetation, trees, shrubs, and Megascans library assets effectively.
Create basic landscapes, terrain surfaces, and realistic architectural site context.
Populate architectural scenes with scale-appropriate people, characters, and vehicles.
Manage scene asset density, polygon complexity, and real-time viewport performance.
Set up architectural cameras with balanced height, field of view, and vertical perspective.
Compose professional architectural still images following photography principles.
Animate smooth camera movement and keyframe transitions through architectural spaces.
Build and export a polished 30–60-second architectural walkthrough video.
Distinguish between Standard Real-Time, Lumen, and hardware-accelerated Path Tracer modes.
Package local interactive presentations using Twinmotion Presenter for client review.
Understand Twinmotion Cloud subscription requirements and VR hardware considerations.
Export high-resolution still images and video sequences with standardized naming.
Perform visualization quality assurance audits to detect clipping, light leaks, and scale errors.
Package editable Twinmotion (.tm) project archives with all external asset dependencies.
Prepare comprehensive client handover guides, revision logs, and compatibility notes.

portfolio.title: Twinmotion Architectural Visualization & Interactive Walkthrough Portfolio
portfolio.name: Twinmotion Architectural Visualization & Interactive Walkthrough Portfolio
portfolio.description: One coordinated architectural visualization capstone based on a supplied residential or commercial model, containing four finished architectural stills, day/evening lighting treatments, a 30–60-second walkthrough video, a local interactive presentation, and an editable Twinmotion project archive.

deliverable_01.name: Four Finished Architectural Images
deliverable_01.scope: Four high-resolution architectural still images communicating design intent and spatial quality.
image_set: Image 01: Exterior Hero View — Strong architectural framing, realistic facade materials, and daytime lighting.
Image 02: Alternative Architectural View — Secondary elevation or angled perspective highlighting building form and context.
Image 03: Interior or Featured Space — Eye-level perspective with balanced lighting, materials, and human scale.
Image 04: Detail or Atmospheric View — Close-up architectural detail, landscape composition, or evening atmosphere.
requirements: High-resolution still image exports (1080p minimum, 4K supported where hardware permits)
Accurate architectural camera composition with straight vertical lines
Realistic PBR materials with proper texture scale and roughness
Contextual landscape and environment population supporting the architecture

deliverable_02.name: Day & Evening Lighting Variations
deliverable_02.scope: Two distinct lighting treatments applied to the same architectural scene.
deliverable_02.treatment_a: Daytime Treatment — Natural sunlight, clear or partly cloudy dynamic sky, and balanced natural exposure.
deliverable_02.treatment_b: Evening Treatment — Sunset or twilight sky, warm interior luminaire activation (2700K–3000K), and exterior landscape lighting.
requirements: Same core architectural scene and consistent camera framing for direct comparison
Distinct daylight and artificial lighting moods with realistic shadow falloff
Side-by-side comparative presentation sheet documenting lighting settings

deliverable_03.name: Architectural Walkthrough Video
requirements: Clear narrative route: establishing exterior view → approach/entry → primary space → closing view
Smooth camera motion without sudden speed changes or collisions through geometry
Stable framing with consistent focal length and comfortable eye-level height (1.5m–1.7m)
Exported at 1080p (or higher), 30fps/60fps, in MP4 format with smooth playback
evidence: Keyframe sequence and camera path timeline screenshot
Video export settings and playback quality review

deliverable_04.name: Local Interactive Presentation
deliverable_04.scope: Standalone Twinmotion Presenter package allowing interactive client navigation of saved views.
requirements: Organized media set: includes final stills, day/evening treatments, and walkthrough
Configured viewing modes (guided viewpoints and controlled free walk)
Working local executable package (Windows .exe or macOS .app where supported)
Client viewing instructions and system hardware requirement sheet
deliverable_04.fallback: If local executable export is restricted by platform or hardware, students present an in-project interactive presentation demo with recorded navigation and documented constraints.

deliverable_05.name: Editable Project & Client Handover
handover_package: 2. Source architectural model file where redistribution is authorized
3. Four final high-resolution architectural still images (PNG / JPG)
4. Day and evening lighting comparative presentation sheet
6. Local Twinmotion Presenter executable package or documented supported fallback
7. Imported asset manifest and Datasmith link configuration notes
9. Camera configuration and focal length documentation
10. Render quality and export settings sheet
11. Scene performance and optimization notes (FPS and polygon footprint)
12. Client handover guide with navigation instructions
13. Project revision log recording mentor critique and adjustments
14. Project compatibility and hardware requirement notes

faq.question: Is Twinmotion suitable for beginners?
faq.answer: Yes. The course introduces Twinmotion's interface, model-import workflows, materials, lighting, and real-time architectural presentation skills from the ground up.

faq.question: Do I need 3D modeling experience?
faq.answer: Basic 3D spatial understanding is helpful. Advanced modeling experience is not mandatory when prepared 3D models are supplied for all exercises.

faq.question: What will I learn?
faq.answer: You will learn model importing, material refinement, lighting, HDRI, environmental assets, landscaping, camera animation, architectural walkthroughs, and interactive presentation workflows.

faq.question: Will I learn SketchUp, Revit or 3ds Max?
faq.answer: The course teaches how existing models from supported applications can be used in Twinmotion via Datasmith. It does not teach complete modeling workflows for all three applications.

faq.question: What portfolio project will I create?
faq.answer: One coordinated architectural visualization project with four finished images, day/evening lighting treatments, a 30–60-second walkthrough, a supported local interactive presentation, and editable project files.

faq.question: Will I learn architectural walkthroughs?
faq.answer: Yes. You will plan camera paths, create smooth animations, and export a polished 30–60-second architectural walkthrough video.

faq.question: Will I learn landscape visualization?
faq.answer: Yes. The course includes vegetation, terrain context, people, vehicles, and other assets used to create convincing architectural environments.

faq.question: Will I learn Lumen and Nanite?
faq.answer: You will learn the concepts and relevant Twinmotion workflows. Advanced feature use depends on hardware and supported software capabilities.

faq.question: Does Twinmotion support Path Tracer?
faq.answer: Yes, on supported hardware and operating systems (DirectX 12 / DXR GPUs on Windows). It is optional in this course and not required for assessment.

faq.question: Is Twinmotion free?
faq.answer: Eligible students, educators, and certain individuals or smaller businesses may use Twinmotion without a paid seat under Epic's current licensing terms. Other commercial use cases and cloud access may require paid subscriptions.

faq.question: Is Twinmotion Cloud included?
faq.answer: Twinmotion Cloud is not included with free Twinmotion access. Cloud presentation features depend on a qualifying paid subscription and are kept optional.

faq.question: Will I learn interactive presentations?
faq.answer: Yes. The course includes local presentations using Twinmotion Presenter where supported software and hardware permit, with a documented fallback for incompatible environments.

faq.question: Will I learn VR walkthroughs?
faq.answer: VR is introduced as an optional advanced presentation capability. A VR headset is not mandatory to complete the certification.

faq.question: Can I use my existing architectural models?
faq.answer: Yes, provided the model format, source software, permissions, and import workflow are compatible with Twinmotion.

faq.question: Is this course different from V-Ray?
faq.answer: Yes. V-Ray focuses on high-end photorealistic still rendering and lighting. Twinmotion emphasizes real-time architectural visualization, environments, walkthrough videos, and interactive presentations.

faq.question: Will I receive editable project files?
faq.answer: Students create and submit editable Twinmotion projects (.tm), organized assets, and documented final presentations.

faq.question: What is the duration and fee?
faq.answer: The course lasts five weeks, includes 40 guided learning hours, and has a listed fee of ₹6,900, subject to Nova Skills' verified pricing and tax policy.
